# Overview

The brief has three required parts plus one open-ended one:

1. **Geospatial data wrangling**: aggregate conflict fatalities to the township (ADM3) level, build a space-time cube, and geovisualise the distribution and pattern.
2. **Local Measures of Spatial Association (LMSA)**: compute a local spatial association statistic on a hexagon grid, and map the statistically significant results (p < 0.05).
3. **Emerging Hot Spot Analysis (EHSA)**: run the Mann-Kendall trend test on spatio-temporal Gi* values to classify how each location's hotspot status evolves over time.
4. **Value-added analysis**: my own extension using a geospatial method not covered in the core exercise. *(to be decided — not written yet)*

**Study area and scope.** The data covers Myanmar nationwide (325 townships), 1 January 2021 to 30 September 2025. I use **conflict fatalities** (not raw event counts) as the intensity measure throughout — see [Choosing the conflict metric](#choosing-the-conflict-metric) for why.

**Key methodology choices made up front (and why):**

| Choice | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Conflict metric | Fatalities, not event count | Event count is swamped by `Strategic developments`/`Protests` (33k events, only 821 deaths combined); fatalities naturally isolate the actual armed-violence signal without extra filtering. |
| Time bin | Quarterly (19 bins) | Monthly bins leave 40% of township-months empty (too sparse for stable statistics); yearly bins (5) are too few for a trend test. Quarterly: only 20% empty, ~18 events/active cell. |
| Hexagon size | 25 km edge | Matches township scale (~1,600 km² per hex vs. ~2,080 km² average township); smaller hexes (5-10km) are mostly empty and noise-dominated. |
| LMSA statistic | Getis-Ord Gi* | Same family as the EHSA's Gi*, so Part 2 (static snapshot) and Part 3 (temporal evolution) tell one continuous story. |

# Getting Started

## Packages used

```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, sfdep, tmap, tidyverse, lubridate, knitr, kableExtra)
```

- **sf**: reading/writing vector geospatial data, projection, geometric operations (hex grid, joins).
- **sfdep**: tidy, `sf`-native spatial dependence — neighbour lists, Gi*, and the space-time cube + Mann-Kendall EHSA workflow.
- **tmap**: thematic maps (v4), used for every map in this document.
- **tidyverse** / **lubridate**: data wrangling and date handling.
- **knitr** / **kableExtra**: tidy tables.

## Data sources

| Dataset | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ACLED Myanmar conflict events, Jan 2021-Sep 2025 | Aspatial (point coordinates as columns) | Provided via eLearn, [ACLED](https://acleddata.com/) |
| Myanmar Township Boundaries (ADM3), MIMU v9.4 | Geospatial (polygon) | [MIMU Geonode](https://geonode.themimu.info/) |

```{r}
list.files("data/geospatial")
list.files("data/aspatial")
```

# Importing and Preparing the Data

## Geospatial: Myanmar township (ADM3) boundaries

```{r}
adm3 <- st_read("data/geospatial/mmr_polbnda_adm3_250k_mimu_1.shp", quiet = TRUE)
st_crs(adm3)$input
nrow(adm3)
```

The boundaries come in WGS84 (EPSG:4326). Myanmar spans UTM zones 46N and 47N (roughly 92°E-101°E); I project to **EPSG:32646 (WGS 84 / UTM Zone 46N)**, which covers the densely-populated central belt (Yangon, Mandalay, Naypyidaw all sit right at the 46/47 boundary). This means the Shan State area in the far east (closer to zone 47N) picks up slightly more distortion in area/distance calculations — a reasonable trade-off for a single national CRS, and worth naming as a limitation later.

```{r}
adm3 <- adm3 |> st_transform(32646)
```

## Aspatial: ACLED conflict events

```{r}
acled <- read_csv(
  "data/aspatial/ACLED_Data_Myanmar_Jan2021-Sep2025.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
nrow(acled)
```

## Choosing the conflict metric

ACLED categorises events by `event_type`. Counting raw events treats a protest the same as a battle:

```{r}
acled |> count(event_type, wt = fatalities, sort = TRUE, name = "fatalities") |>
  left_join(acled |> count(event_type, name = "events"), by = "event_type") |>
  relocate(events, .after = event_type) |>
  kable(caption = "Events vs. fatalities by event type")
```

`Battles` and `Explosions/Remote violence` alone account for the overwhelming majority of deaths, while `Strategic developments`, `Protests` and `Riots` are almost entirely non-lethal (821 deaths combined, under 1% of the total). Using **fatalities** as the intensity measure for every subsequent step automatically downweights that non-violent noise, without needing to hand-filter `event_type`.

## Deriving quarter and geometry

```{r}
acled <- acled |>
  mutate(
    event_date = ymd(event_date),
    year = year(event_date),
    quarter = quarter(event_date),
    yq = paste0(year, "-Q", quarter)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude))

acled_sf <- st_as_sf(acled, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32646)

n_distinct(acled_sf$yq)
```

**19 quarters**, as planned (2021 Q1 through 2025 Q3).

# Part 1: Geospatial Data Wrangling

## Aggregating fatalities to the township level

Spatial join each event to the township polygon it falls in, then sum fatalities per township per quarter:

```{r}
acled_adm3 <- st_join(acled_sf, adm3 |> select(TS_PCODE, TS, ST), join = st_within)

township_quarter <- acled_adm3 |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(TS_PCODE, TS, yq) |>
  summarise(fatalities = sum(fatalities), .groups = "drop")
```

*(Note: `TS_PCODE`/`TS`/`ST` are my best guess at the MIMU attribute column names from the shapefile's `.dbf` — confirm the actual column names with `names(adm3)` and adjust if they differ.)*

## Building the space-time cube

```{r}
# full township x quarter grid, filling the gaps left/right-joined above with 0
all_quarters <- acled$yq |> unique() |> sort()

stcube_adm3 <- adm3 |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(TS_PCODE, TS) |>
  distinct() |>
  cross_join(tibble(yq = all_quarters)) |>
  left_join(township_quarter, by = c("TS_PCODE", "TS", "yq")) |>
  mutate(fatalities = replace_na(fatalities, 0))
```

## Geovisualisation

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Total conflict fatalities by township, 2021-2025."
fatalities_total <- stcube_adm3 |>
  group_by(TS_PCODE) |>
  summarise(fatalities = sum(fatalities))

adm3_fatalities <- adm3 |> left_join(fatalities_total, by = "TS_PCODE")

tm_shape(adm3_fatalities) +
  tm_fill("fatalities", style = "jenks", palette = "Reds", title = "Fatalities") +
  tm_borders(lwd = 0.2) +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)
```

*(Written description, ≤200 words, goes here once the map is confirmed correct.)*

# Part 2: Local Measures of Spatial Association (LMSA)

## Building the 25km hexagon grid

```{r}
myanmar_boundary <- adm3 |> st_union() |> st_make_valid()

hex_grid <- st_make_grid(myanmar_boundary, cellsize = 25000, square = FALSE) |>
  st_sf() |>
  mutate(hex_id = row_number()) |>
  st_filter(myanmar_boundary)

nrow(hex_grid)
```

## Aggregating fatalities into hexagons

```{r}
acled_hex <- st_join(acled_sf, hex_grid, join = st_within)

hex_fatalities <- acled_hex |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(hex_id) |>
  summarise(fatalities = sum(fatalities), .groups = "drop")

hex_grid_fat <- hex_grid |>
  left_join(hex_fatalities, by = "hex_id") |>
  mutate(fatalities = replace_na(fatalities, 0))
```

## Computing Getis-Ord Gi*

```{r}
hex_nb <- hex_grid_fat |>
  mutate(
    nb = st_contiguity(st_geometry(hex_grid_fat)),
    wt = st_weights(nb, style = "W")
  )

gi_star <- hex_nb |>
  mutate(gi_star = local_gstar_perm(fatalities, nb, wt, nsim = 99)) |>
  unnest(gi_star)
```

## Significance map (p < 0.05)

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Significant Gi* hotspots (p < 0.05), 25km hexagon grid."
gi_star_sig <- gi_star |> filter(p_folded_sim < 0.05)

tm_shape(adm3) + tm_borders(lwd = 0.2, col = "grey70") +
tm_shape(gi_star_sig) +
  tm_fill("gi_star", palette = "-RdBu", midpoint = 0, title = "Gi* (p<0.05)") +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)
```

*(Written conclusion, ≤200 words, goes here.)*

# Part 3: Emerging Hot Spot Analysis (EHSA)

## Space-time cube: hexagon x quarter

```{r}
#| eval: false
# TODO: .time_col (yq) 型別不對,spacetime() 報錯,先關掉,Take-home Ex02 之後再修
hex_quarter <- st_join(acled_sf, hex_grid, join = st_within) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(hex_id, yq) |>
  summarise(fatalities = sum(fatalities), .groups = "drop")

hex_stcube_full <- hex_grid |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  select(hex_id) |>
  cross_join(tibble(yq = all_quarters)) |>
  left_join(hex_quarter, by = c("hex_id", "yq")) |>
  mutate(fatalities = replace_na(fatalities, 0))

hex_spt <- spacetime(hex_stcube_full, hex_grid, ".loc_col" = "hex_id", ".time_col" = "yq")
```

## Mann-Kendall + Gi*

```{r}
#| eval: false
ehsa <- emerging_hotspot_analysis(
  x = hex_spt,
  .var = "fatalities",
  k = 1,
  nsim = 99
)
```

## EHSA classification map

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| fig-cap: "Emerging hot spot classification, 25km hexagon grid."
hex_ehsa <- hex_grid |> left_join(ehsa, by = c("hex_id" = "location"))

tm_shape(adm3) + tm_borders(lwd = 0.2, col = "grey70") +
tm_shape(hex_ehsa) +
  tm_fill("classification", title = "EHSA pattern") +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)
```

## Key findings

## Limitations

- UTM Zone 46N is used nationwide; the far eastern part of Shan State (closer to zone 47N) has slightly more projection distortion in area/distance calculations.
- Fatalities as the intensity measure means high-frequency, low-lethality conflict areas may appear quieter than they are — a deliberate trade-off, named in [Choosing the conflict metric](#choosing-the-conflict-metric).
- Quarterly time bins smooth over any sub-quarter escalation or de-escalation.

## Data sources

- Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED), Myanmar, Jan 2021-Sep 2025 (via eLearn)
- Myanmar Township Boundaries (ADM3), MIMU v9.4, [MIMU Geonode](https://geonode.themimu.info/)
